sec: Pituitary adenoma classification and mass effects

items.q: Match the pituitary adenoma classification to its size criterion — 1) Microadenoma 2) Macroadenoma … A) Less than 1 cm B) Greater than 1 cm
items.exp: Microadenomas are < 1 cm while macroadenomas are > 1 cm in diameter. (Book p940)

items.q: Compression of the infundibulum by an expanding macroadenoma produces hyperprolactinemia through the ___ effect.
items.exp: Pituitary stalk compression disrupts dopamine transit, resulting in the stalk effect with hyperprolactinemia. (Book p940)

items.q: What two primary mechanisms mediate the clinical consequences of a non-functioning pituitary adenoma?
opts: Direct cortical invasion and CSF seeding
items.exp: Non-functioning pituitary adenomas cause clinical manifestations via stalk effect and mass effect. (Book p940)

items.q: Assess the effects of functioning pituitary adenomas: I Functioning adenomas can produce mass effect resulting in increased intracranial tension. II Functioning adenomas produce specific hormonal dysfunction in addition to potential stalk effect.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Functioning adenomas produce hormonal dysfunction, mass effect with increased intracranial tension, and stalk effect. (Book p940)

items.q: A 52-year-old woman is discovered to have a 2.4 cm sellar lesion that stains negative for all anterior pituitary hormones. Her serum prolactin is 65 ug/L. The mild prolactin elevation is best explained by:
opts: Stalk effect from dopamine tract disruption
items.exp: Non-functioning macroadenomas compress the pituitary stalk, blocking dopamine delivery to lactotrophs and causing mild hyperprolactinemia (stalk effect). (Book p940)

items.q: Mass effect from suprasellar extension of a macroadenoma classically produces:
opts: Isolated lower motor neuron facial weakness
items.exp: Mass effect from an expanding pituitary adenoma elevates intracranial tension leading to headaches and visual symptoms. (Book p940)

items.q: Which feature is NOT typically associated with non-functioning pituitary macroadenomas?
opts: Increased intracranial tension from mass effect
items.exp: Non-functioning adenomas do not hypersecrete hormones; they cause hypopituitarism, stalk effect, and mass effect. (Book p940)

items.q: Match the adenoma consequence to its pathophysiologic manifestation — 1) Stalk effect 2) Mass effect 3) Functioning adenoma … A) Hypopituitarism with mild hyperprolactinemia B) Increased intracranial tension C) Autonomous hormone overproduction
items.exp: Stalk effect leads to hypopituitarism and prolactinemia; mass effect increases intracranial tension; functioning tumors cause hormonal dysfunction. (Book p940)

items.q: A pituitary adenoma measuring 0.7 cm on coronal MRI is designated as a ___.
items.exp: An adenoma under 1 cm is categorized as a microadenoma. (Book p940)

items.q: Involvement of the pituitary stalk by a large sellar tumor can directly cause hypopituitarism and:
items.exp: Stalk effect causes hypopituitarism and hyperprolactinemia due to loss of tonic dopamine inhibition. (Book p940)

items.q: Assess the characteristics of pituitary mass lesions: I Non-functioning adenomas frequently go unnoticed until visual loss or mass effects develop. II Stalk compression impairs anterior pituitary trophic stimulation while increasing prolactin.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Non-functioning adenomas present late with mass effect; stalk interruption reduces trophic hormones but raises prolactin. (Book p940)

items.q: A 38-year-old man presents with progressive bitemporal visual field deficits and severe headaches. MRI reveals a 3.2 cm suprasellar lesion compressing the optic chiasm and infundibulum. This tumor is classified as a:
items.exp: Any pituitary adenoma exceeding 1 cm in diameter is classified as a macroadenoma. (Book p940)
